authors: A. V. Kotikov, L. N. Lipatov, A. I. Onishchenko, V. N. Velizhanin
title: Three-loop universal anomalous dimension of the Wilson operators in N=4 SUSY Yang-Mills model
claim: Three-loop universal twist-two anomalous dimension of N=4 SYM extracted from the three-loop non-singlet QCD result (Moch-Vermaseren-Vogt hep-ph/0403192) by keeping the most complicated (highest transcendentality, weight 5) terms with C_F = C_A = N_c; final formula eq. (12); checks: j -> 1 BFKL pole structure (eq. (17), leading term only) and large-j asymptotics (eq. (28)).
scheme: no N=4 computation: extraction from QCD results computed in MS-bar (DREG); the authors argue within DR-bar that transcendentality levels do not mix and that lower-weight terms generated by finite coupling renormalizations do not appear in DR-bar
symmetry_argument: Replaced by the maximal-transcendentality principle: the universal N=4 anomalous dimension equals the leading-transcendentality part of the QCD anomalous dimension (assumption justified by lower-loop observations, not derived).

assumed: maximal-transcendentality principle (the N=4 function has uniform weight 2l-1 at l loops and equals the top-weight part of QCD)
absence of scheme-induced lower-weight contamination in DR-bar
checked_partially: j -> 1 BFKL check only for the first pole term (eq. (17))
large-j behaviour consistent with AdS/CFT interpolation (eq. (28))
two-loop analogue verified by direct computation (S1a.17)

evidence: Sec. 'Method of obtaining AD eigenvalues': assumption that the most complicated part coincides
eq. (17) and footnote: BFKL check and a misprint factor 4 in earlier refs
eq. (28): large-j asymptotics -88 zeta(4)(ln j + gamma_E) - 16 zeta(2) zeta(3) - 80 zeta(5)
red_flags: not a computation in any supersymmetric scheme; correctness at three loops was later supported by integrability (ABA) and by the three-loop Konishi value, but there is no direct three-loop Feynman-graph N=4 twist-two computation in this paper
cross_checks: agrees with asymptotic Bethe ansatz predictions (Staudacher; KLRSV 0704.3586 = S1b record) and with three-loop Konishi from Eden-Jarczak-Sokatchev hep-th/0409009 (S1a.23) and Sieg 1008.3351 (S1a.07, SU(2) sector)
notes: Lead confirmed: KLOV is not a SUSY-scheme computation; the 'symmetry' input is the maximal-transcendentality principle.
